title: Elastic limiter standby reconciliation and graceful limiter outage containment
creator: Asha Patel
description: Summary: During recent production incidents we observed limiter control-plane unavailability in a primary region that caused client-facing 5xxs and a subsequent bulk failover that overwhelmed the secondary region's admission path. This ticket implements an "elastic standby" reconciliation protocol for quota/lease state and a graceful degraded-shed mode so that limiter outages produce controlled, observable shedding rather than hard-deny storms. Goals: 1) Avoid double-spending of reserved credits during cross-region failovers. 2) Provide a deterministic degraded admission policy (soft-shed) that preserves high-priority traffic and SLOs. 3) Enable fast automatic reconciliation when limiter control-plane comes back online and safe backfill without spikes. Context: The system currently uses per-region short-lived leases with eventual reconciliation. During the outage we saw race conditions where clients re-acquired credits in both regions and downstream services experienced overload. This design focuses on minimizing user-visible errors while keeping token accounting eventually consistent and auditable.
proposal: High-level approach: 1) Standby delta logs: maintain an append-only delta log (compactable) for lease operations in each region that can be shipped to a reconciliation service. 2) Ephemeral escrow accounting: when a host is in degraded mode, it moves new grants into an 'escrow' namespace with conservative expiry and lower effective weight. 3) Deterministic priority-filter: soft-shed rules (priority > X, internal autop-runner, health-checks) are allowed during degraded mode; everything else receives 429 with a small retry-after. 4) Reconciliation window: upon control-plane recovery, a two-phase reconciliation runs: conflict detection (idempotent keys + vector-timestamp heuristics) and safe backfill that increments credits only up to pre-failure caps to avoid sudden spikes. Implementation notes: use existing durable append storage (S3/CDC) for cross-region delivery, leverage current lease id format (region-timestamp-uuid) so reconcilers can determine causality, add a reconciliation lambda with idempotent ops. Telemetry: expose reconciliation progress, conflicts resolved, discard counts, and shed-rate metrics to Console. Rollout: feature-flag gated; start with Canary region, then opt-in for dedicated customers, then global flip.
alternatives_considered: 1) Strongly consistent global lease store (etcd/consul): Pros: correctness; Cons: high latency, single-point-of-failure, expensive cross-region writes. 2) Token lease revocation on failover: Pros: simple; Cons: required synchronous revokes likely fail during outage, increases outage surface. 3) Client-side retry windows and token fencing: Pros: reduces server complexity; Cons: client changes are heavy and not backward compatible. We chose eventual reconciliation + degraded-shed to balance latency with safety.
acceptance_criteria: Canary region enabled with feature flag and shows no >1.5x increase in p99 latency for green-path requests
Simulated control-plane outage test (chaos run) results in <5% additional user-facing 5xxs vs baseline and shed rate is recorded in Console
Reconciler resolves conflicting leases deterministically and provides audit log with vector-timestamps for each decision
Backfill does not exceed pre-failure committed throughput by more than 2% during 10 minute window
E2E test coverage for reconciliation logic and soft-shed policy in CI
testing_plan: 1) Unit tests for escrow accounting and idempotent reconcile ops (PR). 2) Integration harness that replays historical token operations and introduces controlled divergence; assert final balances equal canonical snapshot. 3) Chaostest scenario: simulate primary region control-plane crash and validate secondary soft-shed behavior and telemetry. 4) Load test to verify backfill rate-limiter prevents spike. 5) Security review to confirm logs do not leak tokens/PII.
rollout_plan: Phase 1: Internal Canary (team-only) with flag 'elastic-limiter-v2' enabled in staging. Phase 2: Limited production canary for 5% of traffic with realtime dashboards. Phase 3: Opt-in customers on Dedicated; gather feedback. Phase 4: Global rollout with telemetry guardrails and automatic rollback on error budget breach.
monitoring_slos: SLO: overall API availability for tokenized endpoints: 99.95% monthly
SLO: p99 request latency delta during degraded mode must be < +200ms vs normal
Alert: reconciliation error rate > 0.5% in an hour
open_questions: Q1: Is the current lease id format sufficient for vector-clock style causality? (engineering input from Runtime team)
Q2: What default priority thresholds should be used for soft-shed to protect console and control-plane traffic?
Q3: Can we reuse existing CDC pipeline for cross-region delta shipping or do we need a new lightweight stream?
Q4: Should Dedicated customers be allowed to opt-out of automatic backfill?
